_comment: WHICH OF THE FORTY-FOUR SWEEPS ARE WORTH RUNNING, ruled 11 September 2026.
A sweep runs only where the owner or a permit names a HOST WORKS, an ADDRESS, or a place
smaller than the municipality. Where the owner names a municipality and nothing more, the
row stays undrawn without a sweep: the sample of ten already showed what a
municipality-centred sweep returns, and running thirty more to be told the same thing is
AN ESTATE IS NOT A HOST WORKS. Six of these name an industrial estate or a port and
nothing inside it, and an estate polygon has been refused as a position since Subotica.
Naming one does not make a sweep worth running; it makes the entry wait for an address.
EACH SWEEP IS CENTRED ON THE OWNER-NAMED PLACE, read from the extract's own place node —
never an external geocoder, which is a third party's coordinate under another name — and
THE CENTRE IS NEVER WRITTEN AS A COORDINATE. It is scaffolding, discarded when the search
